title: Elastic staffing wedge and unit cost scan (FY27)
overview: Working workbook to map FY27 headcount bands to unit-cost outcomes across a set of pricing elasticity scenarios. Purpose: give product finance and PL leaders a concrete staff-plan that aligns with price moves and expected margin delta for the hosted API and dedicated offerings.
assumptions: Base currency: USD. Planning window FY27 (Jul26-Jun27). Revenue mix baseline: Hosted API 60%, Dedicated 30%, Private 10%. Baseline average USD/token revenue per workload class derived from Q2 telemetry. Salary + benefits burden = 45% across engineering roles, 35% for GTM. Annualization: hires counted as full-FTE for simplicity; adjustments called out in notes. Elasticity modeled as percent change in revenue per-token leading to throughput or demand shifts; supply-side response is headcount resizing to maintain margin targets.

commentary: Key observations: 1) Engineering spend is the dominant lever for unit cost; small cuts to serving infra have outsized effect on throughput capacity. 2) Margin sensitivity is non-linear because commitments and reserved GPUs create step functions in cost. 3) Short-term headcount cuts primarily deliver ~50% of modeled savings; rest requires contractual renegotiation (cloud/GPU committed usage) or product-level load shaping. 4) Hiring pauses in GTM reduce acquisition throughput; recommend paired marketing investment reallocation rather than pure headcount cuts when price compression is modest.
recommended_actions: Immediate (next 30 days): prepare targeted hiring freeze triggers at -5% realized price; create a rapid-cost playbook (redeploy contractors to critical infra tasks, pause nonessential tooling spend). 30-90d: prioritize 3 small infra role cuts if compression exceeds -7.5%, delay non-critical serving capacity refresh; negotiate reserved capacity flex with major cloud partners. >90d: if price compression persists >10%, implement staged GTM reorg and capacity consolidation; present three-budget scenario to the board with binding contingency triggers. Owner for execution: Aisha Patel (finance-ops) and Marco Ruiz (eng-serving-runtime).
notes: This is a working scan — assumptions to validate: token rev mix (by customer cohort), reserved GPU steppoints, and latency SLA-driven buffer capacity. Next steps: run a cohort-level P&L with actual per-customer token intensity and update elasticity inputs with Q3 telemetry. Meeting to review with CFO and Head of Serving scheduled 2026-09-07.
